title: fix(validation): correctly update falsy values from validator
body:
Fixes #6411.

## Summary

- Update `validateParam` when a custom validator returns an explicit `value`, including falsy values such as `0`, `""`, `false`, and `null`.
- Guard the `value in ret` check with `typeof ret === 'object'` because synchronous Ajv validation may return a boolean.
- Add regression coverage proving that the validator output replaces the original request value for each supported falsy value.

## Root cause

`validateParam` currently uses `if (ret && ret.value)`. The truthiness check skips an update whenever a custom validator intentionally returns a falsy value, leaving the original request value in place.

## Validation

- `npm run unit`: 2205 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed
- Full GitHub Actions matrix is green on the current head

## Scope

The earlier documentation change was removed after review; the final diff contains only the validation fix and its regression test.

linked_issues.title: Validation of optional, nullable number where property value is `0` will default to `null`
linked_issues.body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have written a descriptive issue title
- [x] I have searched existing issues to ensure the bug has not already been reported


### Fastify version

5.6.2

### Plugin version

_No response_

### Node.js version

24.11.0

### Operating system

Windows

### Operating system version (i.e. 20.04, 11.3, 10)

10

### Description

When using a schema that defines an optional, nullable number as a property if I send the value `0` then the property is evaluated to be `null` I have added `preValidation` and `preHandler` hooks to look at the incoming body shape and can confirm before the validation step the raw value is `0` and after validation is `null` my schema for validating the model is:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "length": {
      "anyOf": [
        {
          "type": "null"
        },
        {
          "type": "number"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$id": "MyModel"
}
```

my request body sent from client (and during `preValidation`) is:

```json
{
  "length": 0
}
```

my resulting model in my handler (and during `preHandler`) is:

```json
{
  "length": null
}
```

I can't see any immediate ajv options (or issues in their repo) about this.

If I make the property "required" then I see no change.

If I make the property "required and not nullable" then it works but is now breaking my contract.

### Link to code that reproduces the bug

https://gist.github.com/cmcnicholas/cc83f261bb9cbd6847c901e7c1482b92

### Expected Behavior

I would expect that sending explicit `0` value to a validated model property should retain that value and not default to `null`
